newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: FOCUS - Sporitelna 1996 net profit surges.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Sporitelna 1996 net profit surges.

text.p: Ceska Sporitelna a.s., the Czech Republic's largest savings bank, expects 1996 net profit to hit 2.1 billion crowns ($80.27 million), against 263 million in 1995, chief executive Jaroslav Klapal said on Thursday.
Klapal told a news conference the bank was likely to pay a higher dividend in 1996 than its five crown per share dividend for last year, but would not specify the amount of the rise.
But analysts said questions remained over the bank's murky ownership structure, and the stock was currently overvalued.

Sporitelna's 1995 post-tax profit, calculated according to Czech accounting standards, plunged to 263 million crowns from 980 million crowns the previous year, after the bank provisioned heavily for risky loans.
The bank's 1995 gross profit was 9.17 billion crowns but it assigned almost an identical sum, 9.13 billion, to its reserves covering "classified" loans -- those which are unlikely to be recovered.
Klapal forecast gross profit of "at least" 6.1 billion crowns for 1996.
Analysts agreed the financial situation of the bank was markedly better this year than last, but said the bank's shares -- which rose 16 crowns to 351 crowns on Thursday -- were overvalued.

Sporitelna has repeatedly refused requests to publish its current shareholder structure. The state-run National Property Fund says it holds 45 percent, while the financial group Motoinvest earlier this summer said it had roughly 10 percent.

"Considering the stucture of owners, and its unfinished privatisation, I expect it's possible the (Sporitelna) share price will fluctuate for a fairly long term above its intrinsic value," said analyst Pavel Sobisek at Zivnostensa Banka. ($1=26.16 Czech Crown)
